title: The Grothendieck Game and Self-Testing Continuous Groups
authors: Alexander Kulpe, Giulio Malavolta, Simon Schmidt, Michael Walter
abstract: Self-testing certifies quantum states and measurements from observed correlations alone, without requiring a description of the devices that produce them. In this work we establish, to the best of our knowledge, the first robust self-test of the full continuous family of measurements generated by Majorana operators. We achieve this by showing that the Grothendieck game, a two-player nonlocal game in which the players receive directions on a sphere and return binary answers, is a self-test of Majorana observables. That is, any near-optimal performance certifies an entire continuously parameterized family of quantum measurements. We further extend this certification to products of Majorana observables, obtaining a robust self-test of the spin representation of the continuous pin group.
summary: This paper develops a novel method using the Grothendieck Game to perform a robust self-test on continuous families of quantum measurements generated by Majorana operators. By showing that near-optimal performance in this game implies the measurement perfectly implements the continuous family, the authors extend this certification to the spin representation of the Pin group. This advances the field of quantum process characterization from finite to continuous settings.
main_problem: The primary goal is to establish a robust self-test for continuous families of quantum measurements, specifically those generated by Majorana operators and the spin representation of the Pin group.
main_result: The Grothendieck Game serves as a self-test for the full continuous family of Majorana measurements, and this technique is extended to provide a robust self-test for the spin representation of the continuous Pin group.
method: The authors utilize the Grothendieck Game, a nonlocal game, whose optimal quantum strategy is shown to constrain the underlying measurement operators to be close to the ideal continuous family generators.
model_or_system: The physical system involves Majorana operators ($\gamma_i$) generating the Clifford group, and the extension covers the spin representation of the Pin group. The analysis relies on quantum strategies for nonlocal games.
key_observables: The quantum bias achieved in the Grothendieck Game, and the squared norms of the difference between implemented operators and the ideal group generators.
important_parameters: The error parameter $\epsilon$ (for near-optimality), and the dimension $n$ of the underlying space.
main_assumptions: The extension to the full Pin group requires using a 'symmetrization trick' involving random rotations from SO(n) to average over the group structure.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the self-test for the continuous family of Majorana operators using the Grothendieck Game, then extends this result to the entire spin representation of the Pin group by averaging over random rotations, and concludes with a general theorem on isometries for compact groups.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful tools for characterizing unknown quantum processes purely from measurement statistics, which is crucial for verifying quantum hardware or theoretical models without full device knowledge.
